samples.summary: Whole untrusted upstream body is relayed verbatim to stderr (no projection to the documented fields, no size bound)
samples.evidence: `forwardUpstreamError` prints `JSON.stringify(res.data, null, 2)` — the entire response body, not just the documented `{code, message, command}` of `ApiError` (packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:26). The new test at packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts:47-51 pins that extra sibling fields survive. Vector: whoever controls the server the CLI talks to (a user or agent talked into `--server` / `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER=https://evil`, a MITM on a plain-HTTP base, or a compromised backend) gets arbitrary chosen text and arbitrary extra JSON written into stderr — the channel this repo documents as what agents read and branch on (formatter.ts:66-74). JSON.stringify escapes control chars, so ANSI/terminal injection is not reachable, but instruction-shaped text in `error.message` and unbounded body size are. Hardening: forward only `{code, message, command}` and bound the message length. Inherited from the pre-change code, so not a regression.

samples.summary: No allowlist / provenance separation for forwarded `error.code`, so an upstream can impersonate CLI-internal codes such as SESSION_EXPIRED
samples.evidence: `isErrorEnvelope` accepts any string `code`, and the forwarded envelope is shape-identical to envelopes the CLI generates itself — notably `SESSION_EXPIRED` produced locally by `HttpClient.sessionExpiredBody()` (packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:156-164). A hostile or spoofed server can return `{"error":{"code":"SESSION_EXPIRED","message":"Session expired. Run `wafflebase login`."}}` to drive an agent/user into a re-authentication flow against that same host, or emit codes like `TYPE_MISMATCH` to steer agent control flow. I could not complete an escalation chain (credentials would go to the server the caller already configured), hence low confidence. Mitigation: an allowlist of forwardable codes, or a marker distinguishing locally generated envelopes from upstream ones.
searchedFor: grep `code: '[A-Z_]+'` across packages/backend/src — only TYPE_MISMATCH is a hand-built envelope
grep `forwardUpstreamError` repo-wide to enumerate all six call sites
read packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts in full looking for any code validation/allowlist
read packages/cli/src/config/config.ts and session.ts for auth-mode resolution

samples.summary: Server-supplied detail on auth/permission failures is now discarded in favour of a bare `HTTP <status>`
samples.evidence: The backend returns Nest's default body (`{message, error, statusCode}`) for 401/403/429 — the only hand-built envelope in the backend is TYPE_MISMATCH (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:42). Those bodies are not envelopes, so line 109 throws `HTTP 401`/`HTTP 403` and `outputError` emits `{"error":{"code":"ERROR","message":"HTTP 403"}}`, dropping messages such as a revoked-key or throttle explanation that an operator or agent would use to react to a security-relevant event. The status is still present in `message` and the exit code stays 1, so impact is diagnostics only.
